reforms.description: The United States increased government expenditure for basic research and development as part of a broader competitiveness strategy, alongside an extension of the R&D tax credit for another year.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public investment in basic research enhances the knowledge base and technological capabilities that underpin long-term productivity growth and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states that steps taken by the United States include 'an increase in government expenditure for basic research and development' as part of measures to address competitiveness.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant but narrower initiative to boost basic research funding as part of a broader competitiveness strategy. The reform addresses a key input to innovation but is presented as one component among several policy measures.
reforms.source_quote: Steps taken by the United States include: federal deficit control, as embodied in the Budget Act; an increase in government expenditure for basic research and development; an extension of the R&D tax credit for another year.
